'''Peter Beyer''' (born 9 May 1952) is a German [[professor]] for [[cell biology]] at the [[University of Freiburg Faculty of Biology|Faculty of Biology]] of the [[University of Freiburg]]. He is known as co-inventor of [[golden rice]], together with [[Ingo Potrykus]] from the [[ETH Zurich]].

==Biography==
Peter Beyer studied [[biology]] at the [[University of Marburg|universities of Marburg]] and [[University of Freiburg|Freiburg]]. In 1981, he was awarded his doctorate in cell biology from the University of Freiburg and received his [[habilitation]] in 2000. Afterwards, he was appointed Professor for Cell Biology at the Faculty of Biology. 

Since 2001, Beyer has been Vice-Director [[Plant biotechnology|Plant Biotechnology]] of the Centre for Applied Biosciences (ZAB) in Freiburg.

Starting in 2005, Peter Beyer became [[Principal Investigator]] in the ProVitaMinRice Consortium, a program funded by the [[Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation]] and one of the selected [[Grand Challenges in Global Health]] projects. The project  «Engineering Rice for High Beta-Carotene, Vitamin E and Enhanced Iron and Zinc Bioavailability», designed to further biofortify Golden Rice with other vital micronutrients has been awarded 11.3 Million USD to achieve its goals.<ref>[http://www.bio-pro.de/magazin/thema/00169/index.html?lang=en&artikelid=/artikel/02842/index.html  More than 11 Million USD for Rice Research] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721034718/http://www.bio-pro.de/magazin/thema/00169/index.html?lang=en&artikelid=%2Fartikel%2F02842%2Findex.html |date=21 July 2011 }}</ref> Research is handled by a consortium of seven laboratories in a number of countries.

Apart from Beyer's group the project involves groups from [[Baylor College of Medicine]], [[Michigan State University]], the [[International Rice Research Institute]] and [[Philippine Rice Research Institute|PhilRice]], both in the Philippines, the [[Cuu Long Delta Rice Research Institute]], and the [[Chinese University of Hong Kong]].<ref>Peter Beyer’s CV {{cite web |url=http://www.goldenrice.org/Content1-Who/who_Peter.html |title=Golden Rice Humanitarian Board |accessdate=18 January 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100803004506/http://www.goldenrice.org/Content1-Who/who_Peter.html |archivedate=3 August 2010 }} on www.goldenrice.org [http://www.goldenrice.org]</ref>

==Research==

Peter Beyer’s research focusses on the [[biochemistry]], [[molecular biology]] and regulation of the plant [prenyl-lipid metabolism ([[sterol]]s, [[vitamin]]s [[Vitamin E|E]] and [[Vitamin K|K]], [[carotenoid]]s. Besides basic science the group focuses on applied pathway engineering to improve the nutritional value of [[crop]] plants.
Peter Beyer pioneered the [[metabolic engineering]] of plants with engineering the beta-carotene biosynthetic pathway into rice endosperm, published 2000 in ''[[Science (magazine)|Science]]'',<ref name="Ye Al-Babili Klöti Zhang pp. 303–305">{{cite journal | last1=Ye | first1=Xudong | last2=Al-Babili | first2=Salim | last3=Klöti | first3=Andreas | last4=Zhang | first4=Jing | last5=Lucca | first5=Paola | last6=Beyer | first6=Peter | last7=Potrykus | first7=Ingo | title=Engineering the Provitamin A (β-Carotene) Biosynthetic Pathway into (Carotenoid-Free) Rice Endosperm | journal=Science | publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) | volume=287 | issue=5451 | date=14 January 2000 | issn=0036-8075 | doi=10.1126/science.287.5451.303 | pages=303–305| pmid=10634784 | bibcode=2000Sci...287..303Y }}</ref> which is widely appreciated as one of the success stories of [[Synthetic Biology]]. Consequently, Beyer is PI in the Centre for Biological Signaling Studies,<ref>[http://www.bioss.uni-freiburg.de/cms/92.html  Members of bioss, a scientific centre devoted to synthetic biology] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091128091739/http://www.bioss.uni-freiburg.de/cms/92.html |date=28 November 2009 }}</ref> which is devoted to this novel field in science.

==Awards and honors==

* 2002 European Science Prize<ref>[http://www.europaeische-kulturstiftung.de/preistr_by_name.php  European Foundation for Culture] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091016105718/http://europaeische-kulturstiftung.de/preistr_by_name.php |date=16 October 2009 }}</ref>
* 2006 Voted as "Most notable and influential people in agricultural, environmental or industrial biotech research of the last ten years" by the readers of Nature Biotechnology<ref>Peter Beyer and Ingo Potrykus awarded by the journal "Nature Biotechnology" [http://www.bio-pro.de/magazin/umfeld/archiv_2006/index.html?lang=en&artikelid=/artikel/00698/index.html] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721034736/http://www.bio-pro.de/magazin/umfeld/archiv_2006/index.html?lang=en&artikelid=%2Fartikel%2F00698%2Findex.html |date=21 July 2011 }}</ref>

Beyer has been recognized as a Pioneer Member of the [[American Society of Plant Biologists]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://aspb.org/membership/aspb-pioneer-members/ | title=ASPB Pioneer Members }}</ref>
